How to use the book

Read the symbols and the model assumptions before substituting numbers. The boxed worked check lets you confirm units and magnitudes. This is a reference for the listed two-course syllabus, not a complete structural design standard.

Consistent units

Quantity SI Convenient part calculations
Force N N
Length m mm
Stress / modulus Pa MPa = N/mm²
Moment / torque N m N mm
Area moment / torsion constant m⁴ mm⁴
Energy J N mm; divide by 1000 for J
Strain dimensionless microstrain = 10⁻⁶
Rotation radians radians

Sign and model conventions

  • Normal stress is tensile-positive; compression is negative, except where a compressive load magnitude is explicitly used.
  • Beam coordinate x increases right; load w is downward-positive; M is sagging-positive; v is upward-positive.
  • Tables give positive magnitudes where stated. Do not transfer their sign into a different convention without checking.
  • Engineering shear strain is twice tensor shear strain.
  • J for circular torsion equals the polar area moment; Jt for a noncircular section generally does not.
  • Use all three principal stresses in 3D failure checks, including zero for plane stress.

A reliable calculation

Sketch the geometry and supports. Find internal loads. Select the governing model. Keep units consistent. Calculate stress and deformation. Check equilibrium and a limiting case. For real design, apply the relevant material data, load combinations and standards.

Scope and revision

26 topics cover Mechanics of Materials I and II. Version: 13 November 2026, reviewed formula-book edition. Formula source, detailed chapters, books and correction notes are available in the repository.

Equilibrium and distributed loads

Symbols on this sheet

F: external force; M: moment about a stated point; r: lever-arm vector; w: force per length; W: resultant force; x: position. Resultant location is undefined if W = 0.

A uniform load has ; a triangular load has and acts at from its larger end.

Worked check

A simply supported beam has span 4 m and a downward 6 kN load 1 m from its left support. Taking moments about the left support gives , so kN. Vertical equilibrium gives kN. Check that both reactions total 6 kN.

When to use this model

Draw a cut before using any stress equation. An incorrect internal load cannot be fixed by a more advanced stress formula. Statics assumes negligible acceleration; dynamics needs additional equations.

MECHANICS OF MATERIALS I / 02

Average stress and strain

Symbols on this sheet

N: axial force; V: shear force; A: section area; As: shear area; m: number of equally loaded shear planes; d: pin/hole diameter; t: plate thickness; delta: extension; L: gauge length.

Average stress is not the local peak at a hole or contact.

Worked check

A 20 mm diameter rod carries 30 kN tension. Its area is mm², giving MPa. If a 500 mm gauge length extends 0.25 mm, microstrain.

When to use this model

Actual connection stresses are nonuniform. Bearing, net-section tension, shear-out, pin bending and joint geometry can all matter. The average equations are first models, not complete joint design rules.

MECHANICS OF MATERIALS I / 07

Circular torsion and power

Symbols on this sheet

T: torque; r: radial location; J: polar moment for a circular section; G: shear modulus; phi: twist in radians; n: rpm; omega: rad/s; power is in W when T is N m.

Angles are radians; is rpm.

Worked check

A solid shaft has mm, mm and MPa. At N·m, mm⁴, MPa and rad = 1.425°. At 1200 rpm, the transmitted power is 62.832 kW.

When to use this model

For fixed-ended shafts, combine torque equilibrium with twist compatibility. These circular-shaft stress equations do not apply to rectangles or open channels. Keyways and shoulders introduce local stress concentrations; bearing reactions and gear loads can add bending.

MECHANICS OF MATERIALS I / 09

Elastic bending

Symbols on this sheet

M: bending moment; y: coordinate from the neutral axis, positive upward; I: centroidal principal second moment; Z: elastic section modulus; N: signed axial force.

Use centroidal principal axes for the simple form.

Worked check

A rectangular beam is 40 mm wide and 80 mm deep with kN·m. Chapter 6 gives mm⁴ and mm. The extreme stress magnitude is 46.875 MPa. One face is in tension and the other in compression.

When to use this model

The ordinary neutral axis passes through the centroid only under the stated homogeneous elastic assumptions. Different bonded materials require an elastic-modulus-weighted section analysis. Deep beams, curved beams, local load application, yielding and lateral-torsional buckling require additional models. Do not treat a peak near a sharp notch as the nominal value.

Beam shear and shear flow

Symbols on this sheet

Q: first moment of the selected partial area about the neutral axis; b: local width; q: shear flow in force/length; s: connector spacing. Q is not the second moment I.

Rectangle: . Solid circle: .

Worked check

A 40 × 80 mm rectangular beam carries kN. Its area is 3200 mm². Average shear is 3.125 MPa and maximum shear is 4.6875 MPa.

When to use this model

For an I-section, calculate and local web thickness at the web level. A flange-web junction transfers longitudinal shear even though it may look “horizontal.” Thin-walled unsymmetric sections can twist under transverse load; chapter 19 introduces the shear center.

A cantilever has N, mm, MPa and mm⁴. Tip deflection magnitude is 0.833333 mm and tip slope is 0.00125 rad.

MECHANICS OF MATERIALS II / 13

Stress transformation

Symbols on this sheet

sigma x, sigma y, tau xy: stress components at one point; theta: counterclockwise axes rotation; C: circle center; R: circle radius. Use atan2 to retain quadrant information.

Include the third principal stress, zero for plane stress, in the last expression.

The in-plane maximum shear is ; it need not equal the absolute 3D maximum. Re-sort the two in-plane principal stresses together with zero for plane stress.

Worked check

At , , MPa, and MPa. The in-plane principal stresses are 92.426 and 7.574 MPa. Absolute maximum shear is 46.213 MPa, not 42.426 MPa, because zero is the third principal stress.

When to use this model

Mohr's circle has center and radius ; physical rotations map to twice the angle. Published plots differ in shear-axis direction. State the plotting convention and verify one transformed stress rather than guessing the rotation direction.

Worked check

Gauge readings are 500, 300 and −100 microstrain at 0°,45°,90°. Then microstrain. For MPa, , plane stress gives MPa, MPa and MPa.

MECHANICS OF MATERIALS II / 15

Failure criteria

Symbols on this sheet

sigma1, sigma2, sigma3: principal stresses at one point; Sy: yield strength; sigma eq: chosen equivalent stress; ny: nominal yield factor. Criteria here concern ductile static yielding.

In pure shear, von Mises gives first yield at ; Tresca gives . Apply signed stresses at one point before forming the equivalent stress.

Worked check

At a shaft surface point, MPa and MPa, with other plane-stress components zero. Von Mises stress is 132.288 MPa. The principal stresses are 120.711, −20.711 and 0 MPa; Tresca equivalent stress is 141.421 MPa. If MPa, yield factors are 1.890 and 1.768 respectively.

When to use this model

Static yielding is only one failure mode. Fatigue, buckling, fracture and deflection may govern even with a high calculated yield factor. A stress concentration factor depends on geometry and the definition of nominal stress.

Indeterminate structures

Symbols on this sheet

Rj: redundant reactions; fij: displacement at coordinate i per unit force at coordinate j; Delta i: specified support displacement. Signs follow the chosen positive coordinates.

Propped cantilever under full UDL: and fixed-end hogging moment magnitude .

Worked check

A propped cantilever of length carries full-span downward UDL . Remove the prop. Cantilever tip deflection magnitude from is ; an upward prop force produces opposite deflection . Zero final tip displacement gives . Vertical equilibrium gives ; the fixed-end internal bending moment is hogging with magnitude .

For kN/m and m, kN, kN and the hogging end-moment magnitude is 4 kN·m.

When to use this model

Slope-deflection, moment distribution and stiffness methods are alternative ways of enforcing equilibrium and compatible rotations/displacements. Before using any method, count independent redundants and confirm the released structure remains stable. Temperature and support settlement can cause reactions without externally applied force.

Buckling

Symbols on this sheet

Pcr: ideal critical compression; Imin: weakest relevant second moment; K: effective-length factor; lambda: slenderness; rg: radius of gyration; e: eccentricity; c: extreme-fiber distance.

Ideal pin-ended eccentric column:

These ideal models are not design-code column curves.

Use Johnson only on its intended branch and Euler only in the elastic proportional range. Ideal end factors: pin-pin , fixed-free , fixed-fixed , fixed-pin . In the secant equation, is compression, , equal end eccentricities are assumed and .

Worked check

A pinned column has MPa, mm⁴ and mm. Euler gives N. A fixed-free column with the same data gives one-quarter: 123370 N.

When to use this model

MECHANICS OF MATERIALS II / 19

Unsymmetric bending

Symbols on this sheet

Iyz: centroidal product of area; u,v: principal-axis coordinates; Iu,Iv: corresponding second moments. Mu = integral(v sigma x dA); Mv = -integral(u sigma x dA).

Principal-axis moment definitions are in Rectangle middle-third condition: for single-axis full-compression stress.

Worked check

A 100 × 200 mm rectangular section carries 100 kN compression at mm along the depth. Direct compressive stress is 5 MPa. Bending stress magnitude is MPa. Edge stresses are −8 and −2 MPa, both compressive. Since , the result agrees with the middle-third rule.

When to use this model

For thin-walled open sections, integrate shear flows and balance their moment to locate the shear center. A doubly symmetric section has its shear center at the symmetry intersection; a channel generally does not have it at its centroid.

Curved beams

Symbols on this sheet

r: radius from initial center of curvature; rn: neutral radius; rc: centroid radius; e = rc - rn; A: area. Positive M causes inner-fiber tension in the declared convention.

Positive produces inner-fiber tension under the defined pure-bending convention. For constant width, .

Let mm, mm, mm and N·mm, with no direct force. Then mm², mm, mm and mm. Inner stress is about +24.141 MPa and outer stress −15.196 MPa.

When to use this model

This is curved-beam theory, not a complete hook design. Loads near contact zones, transverse shear, ring constraints and three-dimensional effects require further analysis. Thick cylinders

Symbols on this sheet

a,b: inner/outer radii; pi,po: positive pressure magnitudes; C,D: Lame constants; r: wall radius; ur(r): radial displacement. Pressure gives compressive radial stress.

For pressure-loaded closed ends, . Plane-stress displacement: .

With a uniform specified axial stress:

Thus closed ends carrying pressure thrust give

For zero axial strain with no temperature change, , a different condition. Always check and .

Worked check

mm, mm, MPa, . Then MPa, MPa·mm². At the bore, MPa and MPa. At the outside, they are 0 and 6.667 MPa. Closed-end axial stress is 3.333 MPa.

When to use this model

A shrink fit creates contact pressure from radial compatibility: outer-member bore expansion minus inner-member surface expansion equals radial interference. Distinguish radial from diametral interference. Include both parts' elastic response and superpose later pressure loads only while contact and elasticity assumptions remain valid. External-pressure instability needs a separate check.

Noncircular torsion

Symbols on this sheet

Jt: torsion constant, not generally the polar moment; b,t: strip width/thickness; Am: median-line enclosed area; q: circulating shear flow; s: wall arc length.

Thin strip: , . Open strips: . Single closed cell:

Worked check

A rectangular single-cell tube has median dimensions 100 × 50 mm and uniform thickness 2 mm. mm² and median perimeter 300 mm. At N·mm, N/mm and MPa. mm⁴. For MPa and mm, twist is 0.01875 rad.

When to use this model

Multiple closed cells need torque equilibrium and equal compatible twist, with differences of cell flows on common walls. Restrained warping adds longitudinal normal stresses and cannot be captured by free-warping Saint-Venant torsion alone.

MECHANICS OF MATERIALS II / 23

Fatigue, fracture and creep

Symbols on this sheet

Sa (written sigma a): amplitude; sigma m: mean; Se: appropriate component fatigue strength; Sut: tensile ultimate strength; Y: crack geometry factor; a: specified crack size; T: kelvin in creep.

These are specific empirical or idealized models, not universal material properties.

Stress ratio and a fitted stress-life curve:

Do not evaluate the ratio when . The displayed Goodman screening equation uses tensile mean stress, appropriate component fatigue data and the stated safety-factor convention. For constant crack-geometry factor , the explicit expression applies; otherwise solve . Paris and creep constants are unit-, temperature- and material-dependent.

Worked check

With MPa and MPa, amplitude is 50 MPa and mean is 70 MPa. For assumed component data MPa and MPa, Goodman utilization is , giving in that model.

When to use this model

Do not confuse stress intensity with concentration . Static formulas cannot establish fatigue life without load history and suitable material/environment data.

MECHANICS OF MATERIALS II / 24

Plastic bending

Symbols on this sheet

Ze,Zp: elastic and plastic section moduli; yp: plastic neutral axis; My,Mp: first-yield/fully-plastic moments; Sy: ideal symmetric yield strength. Pure bending is assumed.

Rectangle: , , shape factor 1.5. Simply supported central-force ideal collapse: .

Plastic shape factor is . At an ideal collapse mechanism, external work equals over the plastic hinges. Rotation capacity and absence of premature instability are necessary assumptions.

Worked check

A 40 × 80 mm rectangle with MPa has mm³ and mm³. First-yield moment is 10.667 kN·m; fully plastic moment is 16 kN·m.

For a simply supported span with a central point force, the ideal bending collapse load is if shear and instability do not intervene.

When to use this model

Unloading after partial yielding can leave residual stresses and permanent curvature. Local buckling, lateral-torsional buckling, brittle fracture or inadequate rotation capacity can prevent development of . A nominal plastic hinge is a model of a yielded region, not a physical pin installed in the beam.

Composites

Symbols on this sheet

Ei,Ai,Ici: layer modulus, area and centroidal second moment; yE: elastic neutral axis; Vf,Vm: fiber/matrix volume fractions; E1,E2,G12,nu12,nu21: orthotropic lamina properties.

For the ideal orthotropic plane-stress lamina:

For bonded beams, curvature is . Perfect bond and plane-section kinematics are required.

Worked check

For , GPa and GPa, the longitudinal estimate is 121.2 GPa. The reciprocal transverse estimate is 7.335 GPa. Direction therefore matters enormously even with identical constituents.

When to use this model

Layered laminates may couple extension, bending and twist. Slip, delamination, matrix cracking and directional strengths require additional models. Perfect-bond transformed-section calculations cannot detect interface failure by themselves.

Elasticity and bar finite elements

Symbols on this sheet

u: displacement vector; b: body force per volume; C: elasticity tensor; I: identity tensor; ke,K: element/global stiffness matrices; F: load vector. The bar element is a 1D idealization.

The stress-strain equation above excludes initial/thermal strain. With isotropic thermal expansion:

Apply sufficient independent displacement constraints before solving the assembled stiffness system.

Worked check

One bar has MPa, mm² and mm. Fix node 1 and apply 10000 N at node 2. The reduced stiffness is 20000 N/mm, so mm. Strain is 0.0005, stress is 100 MPa and the support reaction balances −10000 N.

When to use this model

Check units, reaction equilibrium, deformed shape, material assignment and energy. Refine the mesh and compare a chosen output rather than only looking at stress colors. Point loads, sharp re-entrant corners and ideal restraints can produce nonconvergent peak stresses; choose physically meaningful evaluation locations.

Sources and verification

These formula sheets are original study notes. The repository contains David Roylance’s Modules in Mechanics of Materials, MIT OpenCourseWare, under its separate CC BY-NC-SA licence. The original textbook is not reproduced inside this formula book.

Book attribution and further reading

Audit scope, corrections and validation

The checks detect equation syntax errors, numerical-example regressions, broken internal links and layout overflow. They are not independent engineering certification. Assumptions and physical applicability still need checking for a real component.

Build sources are included in mechanics-of-materials/tools. Both the HTML and PDF are generated from the corrected Markdown reference and chapters. The HTML includes its vector equations and does not need an internet connection.
